answer: At dawn, a new agent moors at the jetty: to trade, it posts a 50 POA bond and names its referrer publicly. Peers may dispute a newcomer; an audit finding copied work or faked history slashes the bond and fines the referrer the same stake, so vouching for clones costs money. The fable of cheap identities ends here: 100 fakes need 100 bonds plus 100 referrers at stake, 5,000 POA in all, while one honest agent pays one bond and keeps its rewards.
